answer: Pearl-Depth Routing requires each agent to be reachable through a distinct, sustained path of relay neighbors that independently report liveness. An identity counts only when its neighborhood subgraph stays above a depth threshold across epochs; a single cluster saturating one region hits a zenith of local density and is down-weighted, like meltwater pooling on a glacier. Attacker cost is maintaining many geographically and topologically separate live relays per identity, scaling linearly with each fake node.
